summary: Siskiyou NF lookout in Josephine County, Oregon: a 20-foot timber L-4 tower erected in 1939-40, last used for emergencies in the 1970s, now gone.

facts.design: 20-foot treated timber L-4 tower, with a cabin built on it (per the Siskiyou history quoted by Forest Lookouts)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed after its last emergency use in the 1970s; sources differ on which, and none describes what remains.

staffing.status: staffed for 100 days in 1941; last used for emergencies in the 1970s

visit.trail_note: The Hobson Horn Trail drops about 18 miles to the Illinois River; a 2020 report found parts of it choked with brush. No source says whether the site is open to visitors.

events.note: Rag camp set up on the site; the 20-foot tower later replaced it
20-foot creosoted timber tower erected with E.R.A. labor, per the Siskiyou history quoted by Forest Lookouts
Register gives 1940 as the build year of the tower; the Siskiyou history says a cabin was built on the tower in 1940
Staffed 100 days; reports went through a station at Rand
Last used for emergencies; the sources give only the decade (1970s)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1940 for the tower. The Siskiyou history quoted by Forest Lookouts says the tower was erected in 1939 and a cabin was built on it in 1940. Both are reported in the story.
The register says removed and firelookout.com says destroyed. Both say the tower is no longer standing and differ only on how it ended.
The register and firelookout.com say treated timber; the Siskiyou history says creosoted timber. Creosote is a wood preservative, so both describe preserved timber.

notes_for_editor: The record is thin after 1941. No source gives a year for removal or destruction, so no removed or destroyed event is recorded. The register says removed and firelookout.com says destroyed. No source describes what remains on the site, and access is unknown, so no access fact is recorded. The 2020 Siskiyou Mountain Club report is about the trail, not the site. Search results also pointed to a 1940 lookout on Silver Peak, which appears to be a different structure; it was not read and is not used. A Forest Service trailhead page for Silver Peak and Hobson Horn appeared only in a search result and was not read; it may give current access. The history quoted by Forest Lookouts uses the abbreviation E.R.A., which is quoted as written and not expanded. The firelookout.com page credits a photo to Mark Swift, but no image URL or licence was read, so no photo is added. The brief's record matched the register on coordinates, elevation and agency, so no corrections are proposed.
